capability_investigated:
WhisperProcessor feature extractor with a list input, and the batched
prompt/result contract of frozen.asr_backend.generate (one prompt row,
one result row per input window).
what_i_learned:
The processor accepts a list of raw-audio chunks and returns input_features
shaped (N, mels, frames); generate accepts [prompt]*N and returns N results
(results[i].sequences_ids[0]). The stub fed only the first 30 s, so all audio
past 0:30 was silently dropped — a pure deletion sink on long-form calls.
hypothesis:
Window the full audio into non-overlapping 30 s segments, decode them in one
batched generate call, and concatenate the per-window text. This recovers the
truncated tail that the single-window stub deleted, which should sharply cut
corpus_cer on the long-form 0715 batch.

capability_investigated:
The VRAM cost model of frozen.asr_backend.generate under a batched prompt
list — what CT2 Whisper allocates when given (N, mels, frames) features vs
a single row.
what_i_learned:
generate decodes the whole prompt batch concurrently, so passing all N 30 s
windows in one call allocates encoder+decoder state for every row at once and
OOMs on long calls. Feeding one window per generate call caps peak VRAM at
single-window cost while still recovering all audio past 0:30; the batched
list contract works but is not memory-safe for long-form here.
hypothesis:
Loop the windows sequentially — one processor() + generate() per 30 s chunk —
and join the decoded text. This fixes the iter-1 OOM crash while preserving
its deletion-sink fix, so the candidate actually scores.

capability_investigated:
The `prompts` argument of frozen.asr_backend.generate — specifically whether
the prompt token-id list can carry a `<|startofprev|>` continuity segment
before `<|startoftranscript|>`, and what results[0].sequences_ids[0] returns
that can be fed back as that prefix.
what_i_learned:
generate's prompt is a flat list of token ids, so it accepts more than the
static SOT prefix: prepending the `<|startofprev|>` id plus the previous
window's decoded sequences_ids gives the decoder cross-window context — the
native Whisper long-form conditioning path, which the pipeline had never
used. Until now every 30 s window decoded context-blind from a cold start.
hypothesis:
Carry each window's decoded token ids forward (capped to 200 tokens) as a
`<|startofprev|>` prefix on the next window. Restoring continuity across the
hard 30 s cuts should reduce the cold-start drift/repetition collapse that
truncates windows early, lifting length_ratio and cutting the 80% deletion
axis — strongest on continuous-speech files like the 233 s-span worst case.

capability_investigated:
The timestamp-token channel of frozen.asr_backend.generate's return value:
what results[0].sequences_ids[0] contains when <|notimestamps|> is removed
from the prompt, and how those ids encode audio position.
what_i_learned:
Dropping <|notimestamps|> puts the CT2 decoder in timestamp mode, so
sequences_ids[0] carries timestamp tokens (ids >= the <|0.00|> id, each step
= 0.02 s) interleaved with text — a return-value channel the pipeline was
stripping via skip_special_tokens and otherwise discarding. The last such
token marks where the decode stayed reliable in the 30 s window, giving a
data-driven seek position that the fixed +30 s split never had.
hypothesis:
Mid-utterance fixed-window cuts drive the deletion axis (del 80%, len 0.65)
by forcing cold restarts mid-word that drift/loop and drop tails. Advancing
the next window to the decoder's last emitted timestamp (clamped to a trusted
20–30 s range, else full-window) cuts at natural boundaries and re-decodes
the uncertain tail with a clean lead-in, recovering deleted span while
keeping window count ~1.5x the blind split.

capability_investigated:
The scores and no_speech_prob return channels of frozen.asr_backend.generate:
what results[0] carries when return_scores=True and return_no_speech_prob=True
are passed, and how CT2 routes sampling_temperature (sampling_topk=0 vs the
greedy default of 1).
what_i_learned:
generate's result object exposes scores (a length-normalized average log-prob
per returned hypothesis, scores[0] for beam_size=1) and no_speech_prob (a
scalar) only when those kwargs are set — both were stripped/ignored before.
scores[0] is directly comparable to Whisper's -1.0 confidence gate, giving a
per-window failure signal the pipeline never had. sampling_temperature only
perturbs the decode when sampling_topk=0 (full-distribution sampling); at the
default topk=1 the decode stays greedy regardless of temperature.
hypothesis:
Wrap each window's decode in Whisper's native temperature-fallback loop:
greedy first, and when scores[0] is below -1.0 re-decode the same window at
rising sampling temperatures (sampling_topk=0), keeping the highest-confidence
candidate; no_speech_prob>=0.6 short-circuits to avoid re-rolling silence into
hallucination. Collapsed greedy passes that dropped half a window — the source
of the residual deletion axis (del 67%, length_ratio 0.82) — get replaced by a
pass that covers the span.
